items.title: [codex] Repair Functions predecessor release routing
items.body:
## Summary

This repair addresses the late unresolved review finding on merged PR #1758. The historical issue #1748 Functions builder now distinguishes its three valid active-manifest states:

- exact authenticated issue #1747 predecessor: materialize issue #1748;
- issue #1748 same release: rebuild and validate normally;
- authenticated release newer than issue #1748: validate successor custody and perform no writes.

Malformed or forged predecessor and same-release state remains fail-closed.

Fixes #1749.

## Cause and user impact

`main()` previously treated every active manifest whose `issue` was not `1748` as a successor. In the intended pre-release state, the active manifest is legitimately issue #1747, so `validate_checked_release()` entered its successor path and rejected the release because `1747` is not greater than `1748`. This aborted the Functions materialization before any output could be written.

The first repair still trusted any parseable active manifest with `issue == 1748`. A forged same-release manifest could therefore enter the build loop and be overwritten with canonical output, washing away the invalid input instead of failing closed.

- Restrict successor preservation to integer issue identities strictly newer than `1748`.
- Admit issue #1747 only when the active manifest has the pinned predecessor SHA-256 and is raw-byte identical to the immutable issue #1747 snapshot.
- Admit same-release issue #1748 only when both active and immutable snapshot manifests have the pinned identity and SHA-256 and are raw-byte identical, then use the normal deterministic rebuild path.
